hard_think: Availability recovery is not RSI: a bounded second proof can remove a false negative but cannot propose, evaluate, promote, canary, roll back, or learn retrieval changes.
A self-hashed query receipt supplies integrity and exact binding within the trusted owner process; it is not independent signer authority or runtime exact-closure proof.
The controller proof limit must remain exactly two even if low-level acquisition attempts evolve; lower-level exhaustion is only a retry-admission predicate.
The remaining stage-zero runtime closure and WRE evidence admission must be separate focused transactions.
dialectic_sweep: Retrying every failure would improve apparent availability but would turn deterministic, stale, malformed, or forged evidence into effects; only a verified allowlisted exhausted transient qualifies.
Trusting top-level retry counters was smaller code but permitted forged exhaustion; telemetry had to enter the existing query-receipt digest before return.
Reusing MAX_OWNER_ATTEMPTS for controller proofs appeared consistent but silently broadened controller authority when acquisition policy changes; a fixed local two-proof ceiling is safer.
Increasing the WSP_62 interface or function exemptions would hide candidate debt; documentation was compressed to exact ceilings and the 51-line function was restored to 50.
first_principles: One exact completion may receive no more than two controller proofs inside min(transaction deadline, first proof start plus 300 seconds).
Authority selection time consumes the same proof budget and a consumed budget starts no query.
The immediate second proof requires receipt-bound exact error and acquisition telemetry plus shared-policy exhaustion and an allowlisted transient reason.
CURRENT must match the exact completion generation and freshness receipt; every other mismatch rejects without retry.
This slice is complete only as candidate code and release evidence; clean exact-main live replay remains an explicit post-merge gate.
